Overlay two layers in one mesh

Source: R/tri_overlay.R
tri_overlay.Rd

Put the features of two layers into one triangulation in which every place they meet is a shared vertex or edge, so that relations between them can be read from the mesh alone (see tri_overlay_relate()).

Usage

tri_overlay(x, y = NULL, x_group = NULL, y_group = NULL)

Arguments

x, y

Layers, as above. y may be NULL to put one layer alone into a mesh (lines or points have no mesh of their own).

x_group, y_group

Groups for a polygon layer (as group in tri_measures()); ignored for lines and points.

Value

A wkpool_overlay: a list with

  • mesh, the overlay as a wkpool_tri (vertex column origin is "input" or "crossing");

  • groups, a data frame with one row per group of the overlay: layer ("x" or "y"), id (the group id in its layer), dim (2 polygons, 1 lines, 0 points);

  • members, a data frame of group (row of groups), item and item2: a triangle row of mesh for polygons, the two vertex rows of an edge for lines, a vertex row for points (item2 is NA except for lines).

Details

A layer is one of:

  • a wkpool_tri, for polygons: groups of its triangles, as in tri_measures();

  • a wkpool of segments, for lines: one line per feature (one line in all when the pool has no feature);

  • any geometry that wk can read holding points or lines (not polygons; mesh those first), one feature per input geometry.

The boundary edges of every polygon group and every line segment become constraints of one constrained Delaunay triangulation of all the layers' vertices and points (cdtr::cdt_triangulate()). Where constraints cross, the crossing point is added as a vertex (computed in floating point, so a relation that hinges on a crossing point is exact for the overlay rather than for the inputs). Each triangle of the overlay then belongs to the polygon groups that hold its centroid in the source mesh, and each line is followed along the overlay's fixed edges. The centroid is that of the largest triangle among those joined to it without crossing a constraint (they all lie in the same groups), so that slivers along a constraint are labelled from a triangle well inside.

See also

tri_overlay_relate()

Examples

if (requireNamespace("cdtr", quietly = TRUE)) {
  ## a unit square as two triangles, and a line across it
  v <- data.frame(.vx = 1:4, x = c(0, 1, 1, 0), y = c(0, 0, 1, 1))
  sq <- new_wkpool_tri(v, vx0 = c(1, 1), vx1 = c(2, 3), vx2 = c(3, 4))
  ln <- wk::wkt(c("LINESTRING (-1 0.5, 2 0.5)", "LINESTRING (2 2, 3 3)"))
  ov <- tri_overlay(sq, ln)
  ov$groups
  tri_overlay_relate(ov)
}
#>   x y    relate
#> 1 1 1 1F20F1102
